title: The Way of the Sage
content_zh:
All things arise, and he does not turn away from them.
He creates but does not possess.
He acts but does not rely on his own ability.
He accomplishes his task but does not claim credit.
It is precisely because he does not claim credit
That his accomplishment remains with him.
Chapter 3: Do not exalt the worthy, and people will not compete.
Do not value goods that are hard to come by,
And people will not steal.
Do not display objects of desire,
And people's hearts will not be disturbed.
Therefore the sage's governance:
Empties their minds, fills their bellies,
Weakens their ambitions, strengthens their bones.
He causes the people to be without knowledge
And without desire.
Thus the clever do not dare to act.
Practice non-action, and nothing remains ungoverned.
